priorities.topic: Rare-Earth-Free Electric Motors and the Future of Transit Electrification
priorities.angle: Today's #6 HN story — 'Electric motors with no rare earths' — has direct, underreported implications for transit. EV bus fleets and light rail traction systems are among the largest buyers of rare-earth permanent magnets (neodymium, dysprosium). China controls 85%+ of global rare earth refining; supply chain disruptions routinely stall fleet electrification programs. Examine the technology (switched reluctance, ferrite-based, wound-rotor designs), where transit agencies are in their electrification timelines, and what rare-earth independence would mean for procurement costs and geopolitical resilience. Include LA Metro, Chicago CTA, and NYCT zero-emission bus programs as case studies.
priorities.rationale: Time-sensitive news hook from HN today. Directly bridges transit electrification (core niche) with supply chain geopolitics (trending). No overlap with existing content — we covered electric axial flux motors but not rare-earth-free technology. Strong evergreen value beyond the news cycle. priorities.topic: US Government AI Model Access Restrictions: What Transit Agencies Need to Know
priorities.angle: HN today: 'Statement on US government directive to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5.' Transit agencies — particularly large metro systems — have deployed AI tools for demand forecasting, signal priority optimization, predictive maintenance, and natural language trip planning. If federal policy begins restricting which AI models public-sector entities can access, what happens to agency tech stacks built on commercial AI APIs? Examine current AI adoption across WMATA, SEPTA, LA Metro, and MTA; map the vendor lock-in risk; and explore open-source alternatives (GTFS-RT + local LLMs) as a compliance hedge.
priorities.rationale: Today's most significant AI policy story with a direct transit-sector angle that no outlet has taken. Connects AI policy (trending daily) to public infrastructure operations (our core niche). Time-sensitive — directive is news today. 'Electric motors + AI policy' gives us two strong news-driven pieces today, covering both the hardware and software layers of transit modernization.

priorities.angle: HN today: 'Open source AI must win.'
